chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from one of his companions, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), that he said:
Regarding a man who married two sisters in one marriage contract, he said: He has the choice; he may keep whichever of the two he desires and release the other.
And he said regarding a man who had a slave girl, so he slept with her, then bought her mother or her daughter: She is not permissible for him [ever].
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man marries two sisters at the same time or buys the mother of his slave concubine?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between temporary prohibition (due to simultaneous marriage) and permanent prohibition (due to consummation with a slave and subsequent purchase of her relative). It highlights the Shia juristic principle that while marrying two sisters in one contract allows for the retention of either, consummation with a slave girl creates an eternal barrier if her mother or daughter is later acquired, reflecting the specific application of lineage and union rules in classical fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, fro one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from one of the two (5<sup>th</sup> or 6<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>)

having said regarding a man who married two sisters in one marriage tie. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is with the choice. He can keep whichever of the two he so desires to, and free the way of the other one’.

And he<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a man who had a slave girl for him, so he slept with her, then bought her paternal aunt, or her daughter. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘She would not be Permissible for him, ever’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from certain persons of his people who have said the following: “About the case of a man who marries two sisters in one marriage, one of the two Imam, (abu Ja’far or abu ’Abd Allah), ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘He has the choice to keep whichever he wants and allow the other one to go.’
About the case of a man who had a slave-girl with whom he went to bed, then bought her mother or her daughter, he (the Imam) said, ’She is unlawful for him forever.’”
